column1: # fixture-provenance.tsv — how each validation fixture's field names were established.
# WHY. run-sigma-validation.sh and run-cloud-validation.sh prove a rule fires against OUR
# fixture. Where the fixture was hand-written from the same belief that produced the rule,
# that proves internal consistency and nothing about the provider's schema — a rule keyed
# on a field the provider does not emit passes its true positive AND its true negative,
# then sits inert in production. See #149: npm_malicious_package_publish's TN fixture
# asserts `actor.type: ci` because the rule does, and neither is confirmed against npm.
# This file does not fix that. It makes it VISIBLE, so a reader can tell which green
# checks rest on a verified schema and which rest on an assumption.
# PROVENANCE, in descending order of trust:
#   captured           taken from a real event emitted by the real system. The note gives
#                      the source (Phase-3 capture, a tenant export, a vendor sample).
#   vendor-documented  field names taken from the provider's published schema. The note
#   unverified         written from inference or from the rule itself. Trust accordingly.
# Everything starts `unverified` because that is the honest default: nobody recorded
# otherwise, and Phase 3 (captured fixtures) is explicitly not done. Upgrading a row is a
# real piece of work — confirm the fields, cite the source in the note, change the value.
# check-fixture-provenance.sh enforces that every manifest-referenced fixture has a row,
# so a NEW fixture cannot arrive without someone stating where its schema came from.

CAPTURED Sysmon 1 verbatim - the cmd.exe RogueWinRM.exe spawned as SYSTEM from a LOCAL SERVICE context, Privilege Escalation/RogueWinRM.evtx (MSEDGEWIN10, 2020-05-24) in sbousseaden/EVTX-ATTACK-SAMPLES @4ceed2f4706daf601c212a8f91c113dd85349a2c. The old User-keyed rule fired on NONE of the six real potato captures in the corpus. 104 record shape (Provider Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog, written to the SYSTEM channel; UserData/LogFileCleared carrying SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, SubjectUserSid, Channel, BackupPath) per LogRhythm's EVID 104 reference and Microsoft's event-1102 documentation for the shared LogFileCleared template. Like 1102, the payload sits under UserData rather than EventData. The Channel element inside LogFileCleared - the log that was actually cleared - is kept here because it is really in the record, but be aware it COLLIDES: zircolite flattens on the leaf key name, so this Channel and Event.System.Channel ("System") become one field, and the surviving value is whichever the parser reached first (verified against zircolite v3.7.6 - reordering the two blocks flips it). Nothing rests on that here: the windows-audit pipeline adds no Channel condition and the rule selects on Event.System.EventID alone, so the TP fires either way. It is written down because it is exactly the trap a later filter_* on the cleared channel would fall into

1102 record shape (Provider Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog; UserData/LogFileCleared carrying SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, SubjectUserSid, SubjectLogonId) per Microsoft's event-1102 documentation. Note 1102 is the ONE Windows fixture here whose fields sit under UserData rather than EventData - that asymmetry is real, not a mistake. Nothing rests on it either way: the rule selects on Event.System.EventID alone, so no UserData field name is load-bearing and a flattening difference cannot make the rule pass for the wrong reason. The UserData block is present for the reader and for triage realism
